subject: Follow-up: data handling & access controls — clarifications from today's discovery call
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: data handling & access controls — clarifications from today's discovery call

Hi Alicia — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap and the questions we promised to follow up on after the call, so your security/compliance team has everything in one place.

Meeting recap (brief):
- Scope: evaluation for inference/integrations across EdgeWave products; sample workloads include ingestion of customer-uploaded reports (PDF/DOC), user identifiers (name/email), and occasional PII within document bodies.
- Primary asks: data residency for EU customers, retention windows for derived artifacts and logs, immutable audit/logging evidence, and support-facing access (break-glass) controls.

Open items we need from you to align deliverables:
1) Can you confirm whether the residency requirement is: a) all customer data for EU accounts must remain in EU, or b) only production inference inputs/outputs for EU accounts?
2) Desired retention windows (minimum/maximum) for: raw inputs, model outputs, telemetry/logs, and audit trails.
3) Any contractual constraints on support engineers accessing customer data (e.g., MDR/justification requirements, mandatory multi-party approval for break-glass).
4) Specific logging evidence format you prefer (Syslog, JSON event stream, WORM storage link, or signed PDFs).

Attachments referenced: your note from the call (I attached a short checklist) and a starter RBAC matrix template we can fill in after you confirm roles.

Next steps (proposed):
- EdgeWave confirms residency/retention bullets above by EOD Wednesday (Dec 2).
- We provide a technical appendix (SOC2 summary, audit log export sample, RBAC template) by end of day Thursday.
- Schedule a 30-minute deep-dive with our Security Engineer (Dev) next week to walk the audit artifacts if helpful.

If any of the above needs adjusting, flag it back and we’ll update. Thanks — appreciate the clarity here.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@edgewave.ai>

Cc: EdgeWave Security <sec@edgewave.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling & access controls — clarifications from today's discovery call

Hi Hannah — thanks for the concise recap. A few answers and clarifications from our side:

1) Residency: For regulatory customers we need production inputs/outputs to be stored in the EU region at all times (both at-rest and in transit). Non-production telemetry may be ok to replicate to US for analytics, but production inference artifacts must be EU-only.

2) Retention windows:
- Raw inputs: up to 90 days by default, with case-by-case extension requests (legal) up to 3 years.
- Model outputs: 30 days default, unless outputs are part of a retained record (e.g., legal holds).
- Telemetry/logs: 1 year for access logs; 3 years for audit logs (immutable evidence).
- Audit trails/audit evidence: we require tamper-evident storage for 3 years for any customer-facing audit request.

3) Support access/break-glass:
- Break-glass must be requestable by the customer admin and requires two-person approval inside EdgeWave (requester + security approver).
- Access should be time-bounded (maximum 2 hours per incident) with automatic notification to our security distribution list.
- We require justification stored with the access record and an exportable audit bundle.

4) Logging evidence: preferred is structured JSON event stream with signed HMACs per-batch; WORM links are acceptable as secondary. We can share a sample ingestion schema.

Attached: EdgeWave_Data_Classification.pdf (internal) and a short list of required evidence files (requesting-logging-evidence-list.txt).

Would like to loop in our platform engineering lead for the technical call; cc'ing sec@edgewave.ai for scheduling. Early next week works for a deep-dive — Wed/Thu preferred.

Thanks,
Alicia
Security Program Manager
EdgeWave Analytics
Alicia.Gomez@edgewave.ai

Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling & access controls — clarifications from today's discovery call

Hi Alicia — great detail, thanks. I’ll summarise how Redwood can meet each ask and note where we’ll need artifact delivery: 

Residency:
- We support region-scoped model endpoints and storage. For EU-only production artifacts we can pin customer accounts to eu-west-1 and prevent replication to US. We will provide a configuration guide + a signed attestation for residency enforcement.

Retention:
- Policy engine: configurable per-customer retention for inputs/outputs (defaults and max windows).
- Logs & audit trails: we can export JSON event streams and offer a WORM-backed archive with retention policy up to 7 years if required (we typically default to 3 years for audit exports).

Support access / break-glass:
- RBAC: fine-grained roles (Read-Only, Support-Triage, Support-Access, Admin).
- Break-glass flow: Redwood supports an auditable temporary elevation token with justification and automatic email notifications. The mechanism supports two approvers; we can enforce multi-approver via an integration webhook.
- Timebox: temporary tokens expire automatically; default TTL is 1 hour but is configurable per-customer (we can set 2 hours to match your policy).

Logging evidence format:
- We can provide JSON event streams and attach HMAC signatures for batches; we’ll include a sample export.

Next steps I propose: 
- Dev: prepare sample audit export (JSON) + HMAC example and the RBAC matrix filled with Redwood role mappings (deliver by Thu EOD).
- Hannah: coordinate scheduling for a technical deep-dive on Wed Dec 9 or Thu Dec 10 (30 minutes).
- Alicia/Security: share any legal holds or special retention exception templates if you already have them.

I’ve attached an initial RBAC template (redwood-rbac-template.xlsx) with suggested mappings — we’ll update once Dev confirms.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
